A.explanation: Coherence means a constant phase difference between waves. It is a condition for clear interference, not bending of a wave around the hill.

B.explanation: Diffraction is spreading of a wave past an obstacle or edge into the shadow region, so the TV wave can bend over the hill to the house.

C.explanation: Interference is superposition of two or more overlapping waves to give reinforcement or cancellation. It does not by itself carry one signal around the hill.

D.explanation: Reflection is bouncing of a wave from a surface. The diagram shows the hill blocking the direct path, not acting as a reflector directing the signal to the house.

hints: Notice the wording that the transmitter cannot be seen from the house, so the straight-line path is blocked by the hill and the house is in the shadow region.
Recall what happens when a TV radio wave meets the top edge of the hill - which named effect describes spreading and bending into the region behind an obstacle.
Check the other words: coherence describes phase relationship, interference needs overlapping waves, and reflection needs a bounce - decide which one puts signal behind an obstacle.
walkthrough: Identify the useful information: the diagram shows the hill blocks the direct line from TV transmitter to house, yet reception is good, so the wave must reach a place with no direct ray.
State the physical rule: diffraction is the spreading of waves when they pass an edge or obstacle, allowing some wave energy to enter the geometrical shadow behind the obstacle.
Apply it here: the TV signal diffracts at the top of the hill and spreads downward behind the hill toward the house.

Rule out the other effects: coherence is only a constant phase difference condition, interference needs two or more waves superposing, and reflection would require the wave to bounce off another surface toward the house.
Therefore the signal reaching the shadow region behind the hill is explained by diffraction. This is option B.
